**Numbers** (seed 1): 8 teams/28 games: 6 called off or changed (1 each), 2 never played, 2.4 s + migrations, 6 s wall. 24/120: 12 (2 each), 4 never played, 11.9 s, 16 s wall. 60/300: 30 (5 each), 10 never played, 60.9 s: rounds 40.1 s, final scores 10.5 s, set-up 5.0 s, publish 2.5 s, called-off 1.6 s, tracked 0.7 s. Last lines of 60: `All 7 checks hold.` / `… total 60.9 s. Putting games in rounds took 312 schedule-draft commands: 81.2 ms each in the first tenth, 182.4 ms each in the last.` (tables: e.g. `1. Vantmesa Academy 10-0 606-435` … `10. Vantmesa Prep 0-9 386-567`).

**Findings about the product** (none fixed here):

- Putting games in rounds is quadratic in the product: every draft edit (`editDraft`, packages/core scheduling/draft-edit.ts) replays all the draft's changes and rewrites the whole draft; 300 moves cost 81 → 182 ms each (24 teams: 22 → 38 ms). No bulk "games into a round" command; the import keeps no rounds. The draft is capped at 700 kB (`maxDraftBytes`); at some size above 300 games a season's rounds could be refused (not measured).
- Each final score costs ~36 ms at 300 games vs ~30 ms at 120: standings rebuilt for the whole season on every result. Mild.
- A typed score, a forfeit and a box score carry no overtime count (`overtimePeriods` null, decide-game.ts); only a tracked game's end sets it. So the part-1 tie-breaks typed in as +2 are not known as overtime.
- A forfeit counts as a win and a loss with no points for or against under the default rules (20-0 stored, `countsInPointDifference: false`); the standings and the second working-out agree.
- The web app cannot show a simulated league: its made-up database is built fresh in memory at start (seed leagues, demo league with `LOCAL_DEMO_LEAGUE=on`); it opens no folder. A setting like `LOCAL_SIMULATED_LEAGUE=<size>` using `madeUpDatabase({ simulate })` would make it so (a product change, for the lead).
- All six call-off paths, the overtime and the correction worked first time through the product's commands; nothing refused.

**Choices (technical, mine):** call-offs only on untracked games; their own seeded generator; the forfeiting side is the planned loser; the correction swaps home and away; the overtime game's margin capped at 6 so the 4-minute period holds its plays; times kept on the report's last line only (the tests compare all other lines); 60 teams as its own command, not a test.

# Part 1

**What exists.** In `packages/database/src/seed/`: `simulate-league-plan.ts` (the pure, seeded plan), `simulate-league.ts` (`simulateLeagueInto(pglite, options)`, the play), `simulate-league-check.ts` (`checkSimulatedLeague`, the self-check, and `reportLines`), `simulate-league.test.ts` (4 tests); all exported from `seed/index.ts`. `packages/database/scripts/simulate-league.ts` behind `npm run simulate -- --teams N --divisions N --rounds N --tracked N --seed N` (defaults 4, 1, 6, 2, 1). `seed-demo-league.ts` now exports `putInRounds` (made generic; no change in what it does).

**Choices (technical, mine):**

- Schedule: through the **fixture import**, not game by game through the draft. The draft's own commands take one game a call (`addDraftGame`); the import is the product's bulk door and lands every game in the same schedule draft. Then, as step 2.59 does, the games are put in rounds with `addDraftRound`/`moveDraftGame`, the tracked games are set live with `setDraftRecording`, and the draft is published with `publishSchedule`. So it is still draft-and-publish, fed by the import.
- Results: final scores one game at a time with `games.record_final_score`, in date order (the path a scorer takes each week), not the import's bulk `recordImportedScores`. Tracked games: `openScoringSession`, plays through `applyTrackerCommands` in batches of the protocol's 50, `releaseScoringSession`; the real engine ends them.
- Rosters: 5 players a team made with `createPerson` + `addToRoster` (the tracker's lineup of five). Names: step 2.59's invented school words, kinds, roads and surnames, with plain first names; the plan test runs 2.59's no-real-name check on 140 teams.
- Schedule shape: circle-method round robin per division, one game day a week; the bye takes the fixed place for odd sizes; home/away alternate by place and turn about each pass, so every team is within one game home/away after each full pass and within two between (checked by script for 2–24 teams, 1–40 rounds).
- Results: 52 points ± 6 × strength gap ± 1.5 home edge + luck; strengths +1.5 / spread / −1.5 per division; a tie gets 2 overtime points to one side.
- High-school rules (4 periods; a foul stops the clock, so each period ends on two fouls, not a pause). 20 s of play time per tap.
- The whole play acts at one fixed moment (day after the last game); the tracker's clock is that moment too.
- The command's database is `.local/simulate-db`, deleted and made fresh on every run (so one seed, one league), never `.local/seed-db`.
- Planted fault in the test: the database refuses changing a decided game's score (a correction needs a reason), so the test switches triggers off (`session_replication_role = replica`) for that one update.
- The standings check compares each team's W, L, PF, PA with a second working-out from the `games` rows, and checks the shown order never puts a lower win percentage above a higher; equal ones are reported as "level", tiebreak not judged.

**The report** (`npm run simulate -- --teams 24 --divisions 4 --rounds 10 --tracked 6`, last 15 lines): a header (24 teams, 4 divisions, 10 rounds, 120 games: 6 tracked, 114 final scores, seed 1), five `ok` checks, then the tables, e.g. `1. Briarquill Charter 10-0 632-433` … `6. Ironwhistle STEM 0-10 425-621`, then `All 5 checks hold.` and `Time: league, divisions, teams and rosters 1.8 s, schedule 4.8 s, final scores 3.5 s, tracked games 0.6 s, checks 0.0 s; total 10.8 s` (plus 2.4 s migrations). At defaults (4 teams, 12 games, 2 tracked): 1.4 s plus migrations, exit 0.

**Test times:** plan tests 20 ms; 4 teams 3.5–4.6 s; 12 teams twice + planted fault 9.3 s; the file ~14 s of tests, ~17 s in all.

**Left for part 2:**

- Called-off games: postponed, cancelled, forfeited, corrected (`postponeGame`, `cancelGame`, `recordForfeit`, `reopenGame` exist); they go in at `callOffSeam` in `simulate-league.ts`, and `games-played` must then count the schedule less those called off. Also box-score results, and finishing the season.
- 60 teams in 6 divisions with 300 games. Watch the schedule part: `putInRounds` moves one game per command and re-reads the draft, about O(n²) (4.8 s at 120 games); and each final score rebuilds standings.
- Every public page (home, schedule, standings, statistics, each team, a sample of games) answering 200 with no error text.
- `docs/operations/run-it-locally.md`: how to run it and open the league it made in a browser (the web app would need pointing at `.local/simulate-db`).
- Whether the 60-team run fits GitHub's check under two minutes, or runs by its own command.

**What the product could not do for a season:** no bulk way to add games to the draft (hence the import); the import keeps no rounds (step 2.166), so rounds cost one command per game. Nothing else was missing for part 1.
